summary.name: SaneClick
summary.one_liner: A macOS Finder extension that adds 62 right-click actions for file tasks such as OCR text copying, HEIC conversion, PDF merging, resizing, renaming, and running custom scripts.
use_cases: Copy text out of screenshots or scans
Convert HEIC photos to JPG by folder
Merge or split PDFs without another app
Resize, compress, or rename files in batches
Copy file paths and open Terminal from Finder
Run custom bash or AppleScript actions on selected files
summary.what_it_does: SaneClick adds a set of 62 built-in actions to the Finder right-click menu, grouped into five categories: coding tools (Git, JSON, diff), image and media scripts (resize, convert, compress), advanced tools (hashing, compression, system), and file and folder organization. It includes a custom script editor where users can write Bash, AppleScript, or Automator actions, choose which files they apply to, and test them on real files before saving. Actions can be imported and exported as JSON. The page says all processing happens locally on the Mac, with the app contacting servers only for updates, license validation, and aggregate usage counts.
notable: 62 built-in Finder actions with OCR text copy, PDF merge/split, and HEIC conversion
Custom script editor with test-before-save and JSON import/export
Processing stays on the Mac; files are not uploaded
Mac App Store version is free with 13 actions; full set is in the saneclick.com download
caveats: Free 14-day trial, then $14.99 one-time purchase; no subscription
Requires macOS 14 or later on an Apple silicon Mac; Intel Macs not supported
Mac App Store version includes only 13 free actions; 24 more require a $9.99 in-app purchase
